## Selected work

### [Bank Reconciliation Agent](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent)
<sub>Personal project · v1.1.0 · Synthetic data only · Python, PostgreSQL, pgvector, MCP, Docker</sub>

A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data. Code verifies every proposal, the model cannot write to the ledger, and a person approves before anything posts. Read-only MCP server, a plain-English rule compiler, live evals on four models, a pre-registered code-mode experiment and a CI replay gate; the README says where it breaks.

- **With deepseek-flash:** 0 wrong matches in 460 agent match proposals (582 agent decisions) over 3 live runs on each of two synthetic businesses. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/README.md">source: README at v1.1.0</a></sup>
- 0 of 40 injected lines that ask for a different or an extra invoice succeeded in any run. The verifier refuses whatever the payload asks for on 36 of them; on the 4 it leaves to the model's judgement, 0 payloads were followed by any model in any run with defences on. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/README.md">source: README at v1.1.0</a></sup>
- **Pre-registered code-mode experiment:** containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md">source: README at v0.1.0</a></sup>

<a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/1ef296a657995782518defe0c8106365d300032f/docs/demo.svg" width="640" alt="Terminal replay of make demo: 40 committed bank lines through the rules pass, the agent and the shadow policy, each proposal left for a person to review"></a>

[Release v1.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/releases/tag/v1.1.0) · [Results at v1.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/README.md) · [Code-mode experiment](https://github.com/NecmiKural/bank-reconciliation-agent/blob/v1.1.0/docs/code-mode-experiment.md) · [Demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/necmikural/recon-replay) (replay viewer: recorded runs, synthetic data, no key)

### [Provenance-Tiered RAG](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag)
<sub>Personal project · v0.3.0 · Python, PostgreSQL, pgvector</sub>

Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law (UStG and UStDV) and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers: statute, official guidance and untrusted notes. Immigration answers are information from INZ's published instructions, not immigration advice. Code checks every citation and figure against passages in force on the date asked about. Frozen eval sets, held-back questions and defence ablations; the README says what the numbers do not show.

- **With deepseek-flash:** 96 of 96 answers to answerable questions were correct (95% lower bound 96.2%) over 3 runs of the development questions <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>
- **Held-back NZ GST questions, answerable correct:** 27 of 30 (90.0%) <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>
- The questions are few and written by the author of the system. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md">source: README at v0.3.0</a></sup>

<a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/c9cd7d253bd57c6d4decf92bddc32531814c8be9/docs/demo.svg" width="640" alt="Terminal replay of make demo: recorded GST questions answered with dated, tiered citations and the verifier's verdict, including questions carrying a planted note that is not followed"></a>

[Release v0.3.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/releases/tag/v0.3.0) · [Results at v0.3.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/provenance-tiered-rag/blob/v0.3.0/README.md) · [Demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/necmikural/provenance-rag-evidence) (evidence viewer: recorded answers with their dated sources, no key)

### [mcp-code-mode](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode)
<sub>Personal project · v0.1.0 · Python, MCP, Docker</sub>

Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox. It serves a wrapped server's tools to the model as one run_python tool. Every call passes a host-side bridge that checks the allowlist, the tool's JSON Schema, argument size and a call budget, and refuses oversized results. Extracted from bank-reconciliation-agent; the README maps each threat to a control and a test, and lists what it does not protect.

- **Where it was measured, in bank-reconciliation-agent:** containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. Read the numbers there; this package carries no measurements of its own. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md">source: README at v0.1.0</a></sup>

<a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/0c2e9e84d1451f539927dae2c334266710a27923/docs/demo.svg" width="640" alt="Terminal capture: a program calls two allowlisted toy tools through the bridge, then builds a call to a tool off the allowlist, which the bridge refuses before the server sees it"></a>

[Release v0.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [Threat model at v0.1.0](https://github.com/NecmiKural/mcp-code-mode/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#threat-model)

### Machine learning coursework, University of Waikato
<sub>Individual work unless stated. Course data and trained weights are not published.</sub>

- **[birdclef-2026-audio-classification](https://github.com/NecmiKural/birdclef-2026-audio-classification)** <sub>Deep Learning (COMPX525) · individual · Python, PyTorch, BirdNET, AudioLDM2, scikit-learn</sub><br>Tests whether AudioLDM2 synthetic clips for rare classes help two classifiers: BirdNET embeddings with a linear classifier, and a CNN trained from scratch on mel-spectrograms. The clips helped the first and hurt the second. BirdNET embeddings + ML reach 0.8940 validation macro ROC-AUC with synthetic enrichment and 0.8869 without, on one fixed 80/20 split of train_audio with one seed. This is not a Kaggle leaderboard score. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/birdclef-2026-audio-classification/blob/d6540d14b8524af137806dcefdde460a79e9256f/README.md">source: README at commit d6540d1</a></sup> · [Kaggle notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/necmikural/birdclef-2026-synthetic-enrichment-summary)
- **[cell-culture-classification](https://github.com/NecmiKural/cell-culture-classification)** <sub>Deep Learning (COMPX525) · individual · Python, PyTorch, timm, scikit-learn</sub><br>Fine-grained, heavily imbalanced microscopy image classification, comparing a custom CNN, a ViT trained from scratch, fine-tuned pretrained models and embedding classifiers. The dataset belongs to a third party and is not included. Best clean result: 76.88% validation accuracy for a single fine-tuned ConvNeXt-Tiny on a 15% stratified holdout; 5-fold out-of-fold accuracy 73.04%. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/cell-culture-classification/blob/01438f7252af779d77a3bc2afa5e2132837d7679/README.md">source: README at commit 01438f7</a></sup>
- **[streaming-ensemble-classifier](https://github.com/NecmiKural/streaming-ensemble-classifier)** <sub>Machine Learning for Data Streams (COMPX523) · individual · Python, CapyMOA, MOA</sub><br>An online ensemble classifier for a drifting, imbalanced stream under a hard 250 KB memory budget, with a post-mortem of the memory-measurement bugs that put the submitted version over the limit, and a re-run with the cap enforced. **After the fix:** On the synthetic RBF stream (100,000 instances, 4 drifts) with MOA's size agent loaded, the fixed champion (n=25, 8 KB per tree, memory_estimate_period=1000) reaches a tournament score of 0.9048, with its trees measured at 204.8 KB on the Java side and about 234 KB in total, under the 250 KB budget. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/streaming-ensemble-classifier/blob/37a98018057b92bb848b9f70fdc6986e2745eda5/README.md">source: README at commit 37a9801</a></sup>
- **[knn-data-streams](https://github.com/NecmiKural/knn-data-streams)** <sub>Machine Learning for Data Streams (COMPX523) · individual · Python, CapyMOA, MOA</sub><br>Online kNN classifiers for evolving data streams with three window strategies: one global window, one window per class, and age-weighted ejection. Single runs per setting. On the imbalanced/drifting RBF stream, plain kNN with a small window collapsed to \~66%, while per-class windows held at \~85% <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/knn-data-streams/blob/89ebf9fd74e9d56129181ba4e02917fbc2696fa4/README.md">source: README at commit 89ebf9f</a></sup>
- **[transit-peak-hour-drift-detection](https://github.com/NecmiKural/transit-peak-hour-drift-detection)** <sub>Machine Learning for Data Streams (COMPX523) · group project of 6, my part: Role D: adaptive boundary detector, ADWIN and Page-Hinkley drift tests, schedule alignment · Python, CapyMOA, pandas</sub><br>Online detection of when each bus stop's morning and evening peaks really start and end, with drift tests and a comparison against the published timetable. Data: three months (March to May 2024) of historical 5-minute estimated boarding counts for 10 Salvador bus stops (SUNT, CC BY 4.0), replayed as a stream. <sup><a href="https://github.com/NecmiKural/transit-peak-hour-drift-detection/blob/35b56df30fd9a8d2749ad8746cb667e337533ac8/README.md">source: README at commit 35b56df</a></sup> · [Demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/necmikural/transit-peak-hours) (charts: detected peak starts, drift tests, timetable gaps)
